questions.subject: MSTHC
questions.question: A fixed asset having a useful life of 3 years is purchased on 1 January 2013. Cost of the asset is $2,000 whereas its residual value is expected to be $500. Calculate depreciation expense for the years ending 30 June 2013 and 30 June 2014.
questions.explanation: Annual depreciation = ($2,000 - $500) / 3 = $500 p.a. For year ended 30 June 2013 (6 months): $500 * 6/12 = $250. For year ended 30 June 2014 (full year): $500.

questions.subject: MSTHC
questions.question: Power to a remote transmitting station is provided by a Diesel-generator unit. The original cost of the unit is P65,000. It costs P2,000 to ship the unit to the job site. An additional cost of P3,000 was incurred for installation. Determine the annual depreciation cost by the straight-line/sinking fund method (at 0% interest), if the unit has an expected life of 10 years and salvage value is estimated at P5,000.
questions.explanation: Co = 65,000 + 2,000 + 3,000 = P70,000; With 0% fund interest rate, annual depreciation cost d = (Co - CL) / L = (70,000 - 5,000) / 10 = P6,500.00.

questions.explanation: Co = 65,000 + 2,000 + 3,000 = P70,000; With 0% fund interest rate, annual depreciation cost d = (70,000 - 5,000) / 10 = P6,500.

questions.subject: MSTHC
questions.question: An asset costing $20,000 has estimated useful life of 5 years and salvage value of $4,500. Calculate the depreciation of the asset for the second year of its life using double declining balance method.
questions.explanation: Book value at end of Year 1 = $20,000 - $8,000 = $12,000; Year 2 Depreciation = 40% * $12,000 = $4,800

questions.subject: MSTHC
questions.question: An asset costing $20,000 has estimated useful life of 5 years and salvage value of $4,500. Calculate the depreciation of the asset for the 3rd year using double declining balance method.
questions.explanation: Book value at end of Year 2 = $12,000 - $4,800 = $7,200. 40% of $7,200 = $2,880, which drops BV below salvage ($4,500). Thus, Depreciation Allowed = $7,200 - $4,500 = $2,700.

questions.subject: MSTHC
questions.question: The Farma company provides the following information: Cost of the equipment: $500,000, Salvage value: $50,000, Useful life: 5 years. What is the double declining balance rate?
questions.explanation: Straight-line rate = 1/5 = 20%; Double declining balance rate = 20% * 2 = 40%

questions.subject: MSTHC
questions.question: The book value of the equipment at the beginning of year 5 is $64,800 whose 40% is $25,920. If this depreciation is used, the book value of the equipment at the end of year 5 will be $38,880 ($64,800 - $25,920) which is less than the $50,000 salvage value. Since the asset is depreciated only to its salvage value under declining balance method, what is the depreciation in year 5?
questions.explanation: Depreciation in Year 5 = Book value at beginning of year - Salvage value = $64,800 - $50,000 = $14,800

questions.subject: MSTHC
questions.question: An earth moving equipment that cost P90,000 will have an estimated salvage value of P18,000 at the end of 8 years. Using double-declining balance method, compute the book value at the end of the 5th year.
questions.explanation: DDB Rate = 2/8 = 25%; Book Value at end of Year 5: C5 = 90,000 * (1 - 2/8)^5 = P21,357.42 (~P21,357); Total Depreciation = 90,000 - 21,357 = P68,643.

questions.subject: MSTHC
questions.question: An asset is purchased for P10,000. Its estimated economic life is 10 years after which it will be sold for P1,000. Find the book value at the end of the first three years using the double declining balance method.
questions.explanation: DDB Rate = 2/10 = 20%; Book value after 3 years: C3 = 10,000 * (1 - 2/10)^3 = P5,120.

questions.explanation: Year 1: (2000-500)*50% = 750 (Accum: 750); Year 2: (1250-500)*50% = 375 (Accum: 1125); Year 3: remaining 375 to reach residual value (Accum: 1500).

questions.subject: MSTHC
questions.question: The will of a wealthy philanthropist left P5,000,000 to establish a perpetual charitable foundation. The foundation trustees decided to spend P1,200,000 to provide facilities immediately and to provide P100,000 of capital replacement at the end of each 5-year period. If the invested funds earned 12% per annum, what would be the year-end amount available in perpetuity from the endowment for charitable purposes?
questions.explanation: Total annual yield A1 = 5,000,000 * 0.12 = P600,000; Capitalized cost of facilities PB = 1,200,000 + 100,000 / (1.12^5 - 1) = P1,331,174.78; Annualized facility cost A2 = 1,331,174.78 * 0.12 = P159,740.97; Net perpetual charity fund A = 600,000 - 159,740.97 = P440,259.03 (~P440,259).
